---
title: "Physiology glossary"
---

Use these short definitions to orient yourself, then return to the relevant
unit for the mechanism and its limits. Terms describe a process in context;
similar words do not always imply the same mechanism in plants and animals.

| Term | Working meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Acclimation | A change in an individual's phenotype in response to conditions during its lifetime |
| Adaptation | A heritable feature shaped by evolution that contributes to function in a particular environment |
| Action potential | A regenerative change in membrane voltage produced by changes in ion conductance |
| Active transport | Transport coupled to an energy source that can move a substance against its electrochemical gradient |
| Apoplast | Plant cell-wall and extracellular continuum outside the plasma membranes |
| Assimilation | Incorporation of a resource into organic material; specify carbon, nitrogen or another resource |
| Autotroph | An organism using inorganic carbon as a major carbon source; the energy source must also be specified |
| Chemical potential | A quantity describing a substance's tendency to move or react under given conditions |
| Compensation point | Conditions at which opposing fluxes balance; specify the measured net flux |
| Conductance | Ease of movement of a particular current or flux through a pathway |
| Control | A comparison or reference condition used to help interpret an experimental change |
| Differentiation | Development of specialised cell properties and functions |
| Diffusion | Net movement down a chemical-potential gradient arising from molecular motion |
| Electrochemical gradient | Combined chemical and electrical driving force acting on an ion |
| Endothermy | Substantial use of metabolic heat to maintain body temperature |
| Ectothermy | Predominant reliance on external heat sources for body heat balance |
| Experimental unit | The smallest unit independently assigned to a treatment in the design |
| Feedback | A response that influences the process or variable that generated the response |
| Filtration | Pressure-driven movement of fluid and permeable solutes across a barrier |
| Gross photosynthesis | Photosynthetic carbon fixation before subtracting the losses specified by the measurement/model |
| Homeostasis | Dynamic regulation of internal variables within a functional range |
| Hormone | A signalling substance whose effect depends on receptors, context and concentration |
| Hydraulic conductivity | Ease of water movement through a pathway for a specified driving gradient |
| Meristem | A plant region with cells that maintain the capacity for division and contribute to growth |
| Metabolism | The connected chemical transformations that sustain living systems |
| Net gas exchange | The measured balance of opposing gas fluxes under the stated conditions |
| Osmosis | Water movement across a selectively permeable membrane driven by a water-potential difference |
| Osmolarity | Total concentration of osmotically active particles per litre of solution |
| Osmoregulation | Regulation of body fluid water and solute relationships |
| Phloem | Vascular tissue involved in transport of assimilates and other substances between sources and sinks |
| Photoperiod | Duration of light in a daily cycle; responses often depend on associated night duration |
| Photosynthate | Organic product of photosynthesis, including carbohydrates |
| Plasticity | Ability of a genotype to produce different phenotypes under different conditions |
| Receptor | A molecule that detects a signal and participates in initiating a response |
| Replicate | A repeat whose level of independence must be specified; technical repeats differ from independent experimental units |
| Respiration | Metabolic processes that transfer energy from substrates; distinguish cellular respiration from ventilation |
| Senescence | Regulated age- or context-associated changes leading toward loss of function and often resource remobilisation |
| Sink | A tissue or organ importing assimilates for use or storage under the stated conditions |
| Source | A tissue or organ supplying assimilates for export under the stated conditions |
| Standard deviation | A measure of spread among observations; not itself uncertainty in a group mean |
| Stoma | An epidermal pore regulated by guard cells, contributing to gas exchange and water loss |
| Symplast | Cytoplasmic continuum of plant cells connected by plasmodesmata |
| Transpiration | Loss of water vapour from plant surfaces, principally through stomata in many leaves |
| Turgor | Hydrostatic pressure of cell contents against the wall |
| Ventilation | Bulk movement of respiratory medium across an exchange surface |
| Water potential | Water's potential energy per unit volume relative to a reference, useful for predicting its movement |
| Xylem | Vascular tissue that conducts water and solutes and contributes structural support |

The tutorials introduce these ideas through examples. For background and more
detailed definitions, see [OpenStax Biology 2e](https://openstax.org/details/books/biology-2e)
and the [reading guide](references.qmd).
